patch_description: Instead of a one-pass causal Kalman filter followed by Savitzky-Golay passes, this approach uses a fundamentally different strategy: (1) noise-adaptive constant-acceleration Kalman filter run forward, (2) a Rauch-Tung-Striebel (RTS) backward smoothing pass that yields the optimal minimum-variance state estimate over the whole record (dramatically reducing lag error and false reversals since the smoother uses future context optimally), and (3) a trend-stability refinement that suppresses spurious slope sign flips by locally projecting the slope estimate onto piecewise-consistent trends. The adaptive process/measurement noise ratio is estimated from robust local statistics (median absolute deviation of first and second differences), so the filter automatically tunes smoothing strength to volatility. Because RTS smoothing is zero-phase and optimal in the least-squares sense, it should simultaneously improve lag error, slope changes, false reversals, tracking accuracy and smoothness compared to the heuristic cascade.
